name: MCP registry listing resolution
principle: A listing that resolves is the second clause of the directory mandate, after being listed and before the tool count being true. This file asks it of all 330 entries the official MCP registry carries for CSOAI-ORG, on BOTH surfaces each entry advertises: the package a client would install, and the remote a client would call. The two answers are not the same.

packages.detail: Every one of the 330 packages exists on its registry AND publishes the exact version the listing names. Not one dangling identifier and not one dangling version. This is the surface 290 of the 330 entries rely on exclusively, and it is sound.
packages.probe: for each entry: GET https://pypi.org/pypi/<identifier>/json (or registry.npmjs.org) and check the named version is a key of releases

failures.detail: socket.gethostbyname raises gaierror. The meok.ai apex resolves; the api subdomain does not. All 39 carry a PyPI stdio package as well, so discovery by package still works for every one of them and only discovery by remote fails.

io.github.CSOAI-ORG/gspc advertises https://councilof.ai/mcp as streamable-http. DNS resolves and GET 308s to /mcp/ which serves 200 — as a STATIC PAGE. A prerendered /mcp route is winning over the Pages Function at functions/mcp/[[path]].ts, so POST tools/list returns 405 and no MCP client can complete a handshake. This is B37, and it is ours to fix.

remotes.detail: 40 of 330 entries advertise a callable remote and ZERO of them can be called. 39 name a host with no DNS record; the 40th names our own door and it refuses POST. An agent that discovers us by remote reaches nothing, on every entry that offers one.

what_this_does_not_establish: That a resolving package is a working server. Existence and the named version were checked; the package was not installed and no tool was called.
That the 290 entries without a remote are deficient. A stdio package is a complete distribution and is the surface the registry is built around.
Any download or adoption figure. Package-registry download totals are dominated by mirror traffic and none is claimed here.

coverage.question: The first clause of the mandate is 'we are listed'. This asks it the other way round: what exists here that the registry does not carry?
coverage.detail: 142 unarchived public repositories declare an MCP SDK dependency and are absent from the registry: 61 carry 'mcp' in the name and 81 do not. Publishing them would take the estate from 330 to 472. The work exists; only the publishing step is missing.
coverage.method: Repos enumerated through gh api --paginate users/CSOAI-ORG/repos (CSOAI-ORG is a USER account, not an org — orgs/CSOAI-ORG/repos 404s). A declared SDK dependency is evidence of intent, NOT of a working server: no repo was cloned, installed or run, and no tools/list was called.
coverage.probe: gh api --paginate 'users/CSOAI-ORG/repos?per_page=100&type=all' then for each unarchived repo fetch package.json / pyproject.toml and grep for modelcontextprotocol|fastmcp|mcp[ ; diff against the registry's isLatest names

a_number_deliberately_not_published.why_not: The same diff run the other way says 51 registry entries name no public repo of that name. It is NOT reported as a finding and must not be quoted. Two independent reasons it overcounts: this account exposes 639 public repos against 678 total, so private repos read as missing; and a registry entry's name need not equal its repository's name (`csoai` and `gspc` are both in that 51 and both have repositories). The authoritative figure for dead repository links is 25, established per-repo with gh repo view and published in csoai/mcp-registry-self-audit. A set difference is a cheaper instrument than the one that already answered this question, and cheaper is not better.

superseded_figure.why_wrong: Four answers to one question in one evening: 64, 142, 153, 108. Each of the first three was published with its method and each method was wrong. 64 filtered on the repo NAME, and a name is not a detector. 142 scanned dependencies with a pattern that matched the quoted string mcp but NOT mcp>=1.0.0, the ordinary way a Python project pins it, so it UNDERCOUNTED. 153 loosened that pattern and then matched anywhere in the file, so it OVERCOUNTED: a spot-check of eight found three hits that were a keywords list or the word FastMCP inside a description, not a dependency at all. 108 parses package.json dependencies as JSON and reads pyproject only inside a dependencies array or a poetry dependencies table. Loosening a pattern to cure an undercount is how you buy an overcount, and the only way either was caught was sampling the output by hand.

coverage.detector: package.json is PARSED and its dependencies/devDependencies keys inspected for @modelcontextprotocol/*, mcp or fastmcp; pyproject.toml is read ONLY inside a dependencies array or a tool.poetry.dependencies table, so a keywords list or a description never counts. 362 of 628 unarchived public repos declare such a dependency; 108 of those are absent from the registry.

instrument_disagreement.note: An earlier commit said file-shape and dependency-scan disagree by three. THREE WAS THE NET, not the disagreement: 10 repos had the file shape without matching the dependency scan and 7 matched the scan without the file shape -- seventeen repos, netting to three. Publishing the net as if it were the disagreement is the same error as publishing a subtotal as a total, and it hid the ten that exposed the pattern defect. mismo-bridge-mcp was among those ten.

examples: csoai-x402-wrap-mcp: the word FastMCP inside description
what_a_sample_caught.note: Three in eight. These repos are probably servers on other evidence — but they were counted for a reason that was not evidence, and a number is only as good as the reason each row is in it.
